direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale has elements of 70s thrillers mixed with the goofiness of the era; The microscale is a little goofy, but it is still executed well in the interpersonal scenes; The storytelling feels like a throwback to the 70s mixed with goofiness to make this movie both thrilling and entertaining; They build tension well to show the weight of the situation as it feels like a bomb is going to go off as emotions continue to build up

performance.comments: Has this mixture of unease and goofiness that works well for the character; He accurately portrays the mental state of someone who feels cheated by the system, but also shows goofiness that makes him more relatable to both the audience and the world of the movie; Has pretty good chemistry with the rest of the cast
Shows sense of empathy for Skarsgård's character despite the situation, creating a believable dynamic between the two

Has this soulful DJ performance that you would see from that era; Feels very authentic and effortless as he shows why he is one of the best actors in Hollywood today; Has good chemistry with Skarsgård
Feels kind of like a templated character
Plays his role well as he uses his experience to help elevate the scenes he is in
A little over-the-top, but it feels like an excuse to have him in the movie; It was pretty obvious they came to him to film these scenes

cast.comments: Everyone plays their role well and has decent chemistry with the cast; everyone feels authentic to the era and the situation

story.comments: The concept is interesting because it is based on the real Kiritsis situation; The plot structure is pretty standard and follows the situation pretty closely, despite its Hollywood moments; Character writing is pretty good, as they create a main character that you can empathize with despite his extreme actions, and they do a pretty good job creating supporting characters that are caricatures of the era

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is true to the time and pretty goofy, helping set the tone and keeping you invested; the humor is pretty funny considering how goofy and old-timey this movie is; the symbolism is decently strong as it uses empathy to make you relate to the struggles of the main character, who feels cheated by the system; the foreshadowing is decent

score.comments: Helps set the tone and era of the movie

soundtrack.comments: Helps establish the time period and mood

cinematography.comments: Helps set the style and tone for the era and the situation, feeling like a news 70s broadcast right on the scene of the situation

editing.comments: Helps set the style and tone for the era and the situation, feeling like a 70s FBI thriller

sound.comments: Helps give the movie a 70s feel with its sound design and mixing

visual_effects.comments: Give the movie a 70s feel with its practical effects and minimal CGI

production_design.comments: Helps create the world of the film and establish the time period

makeup.comments: Bill Skarsgård's try not to use his actual face challenge failed again; helps style the time period

review.pacing: Pacing is a little all over the place, but that helps with the hectic nature of the movie
review.climax: Climax is a pressure cooker that finally explodes
review.tone: Tone is very 70s in both style and goofiness
review.final_notes: Saw premiere at Austin Film Festival
review.overall: Overall, an homage to the 70s in both its style and goofiness, this thriller creates an entertaining experience that makes you empathize with the main character in his fight against the system, creating a pressure cooker that finally explodes in the climax
